pairs.fullEnglish: At the end of two years, Pharaoh was dreaming, and behold, he was standing by the river.
And behold, seven cows came up from the river, beautiful to look at and fat in flesh, and they grazed among the marsh grass.
And behold, seven other cows came up after them from the river, ugly to look at and lean in flesh, and they stood opposite the cows on the riverbank.
The cows that were ugly to look at and lean in flesh ate the seven cows that were beautiful to look at and fat, and Pharaoh awoke.
He slept and dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, plump and good.
And behold, seven ears of grain, blighted and battered by the east wind, sprouted after them.
The blighted ears swallowed the seven plump, full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
In the morning his spirit was agitated. He sent and summoned all the sorcerers of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh related his dream to them, but there was no one who interpreted them for Pharaoh.
The chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, 'I recall my offenses today.'
'Pharaoh was angry with his servants and placed me in custody in the house of the chief executioner—me and the chief baker.'
'We dreamed dreams on one night, I and he; each of us dreamed in accordance with the interpretation of his dream.'
'There with us was a Hebrew youth, a servant of the chief executioner. We related our dreams to him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; he interpreted for each man according to his dream.'
Pharaoh sent and summoned Yosef, and they hurried him out of the prison. He cut his hair, changed his clothing, and came before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Yosef, 'I dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. I have heard it said about you that you hear a dream in order to interpret it.'
Yosef answered Pharaoh, saying, 'It is not from my wisdom; rather, from before יְיָ an answer for Pharaoh's well-being will be given.'
Pharaoh spoke to Yosef: 'In my dream, behold, I was standing on the riverbank.'
'And behold, seven cows came up from the river, fat in flesh and beautiful to look at, and they grazed among the marsh grass.'
'And behold, seven other cows came up after them, scrawny, exceedingly ugly to look at, and lean in flesh. I have not seen their like for ugliness in all the land of Egypt.'
'The scrawny, ugly cows ate the first seven fat cows.'
'They entered their bellies, but it could not be known that they had entered their bellies: their appearance was ugly as at first. Then I awoke.'
'I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears of grain came up on one stalk, full and good.'
'The blighted ears swallowed the seven good ears. I told the sorcerers, but there is no one who explains it to me.'
Yosef said to Pharaoh, 'Pharaoh's dream is one. He has made known to Pharaoh what יְיָ is going to do.'
'The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years; the dream is one.'
'The seven scrawny, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven blighted ears battered by the east wind will be seven years of famine.'
'This is the matter that I spoke of with Pharaoh: He has shown Pharaoh what יְיָ is going to do.'
'Behold, seven years are coming, with great plenty throughout the land of Egypt.'
'Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten. The famine will consume the land (its people).'
'The plenty in the land will not be recognizable because of that famine which will follow, for it will be exceedingly severe.'
'As for the dream's being repeated to Pharaoh twice: it is because the matter is established from before יְיָ, and יְיָ is hastening to carry it out.'
'Now let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man and appoint him over the land of Egypt.'
'Let them gather all the grain of these coming good years and heap up grain under Pharaoh's authority—grain in the towns—and guard it.'
'The grain will be stored away for the land (for its people), for the seven years of famine that will be in the land of Egypt, so that the people of the land will not be destroyed by the famine.'
The proposal was pleasing in Pharaoh's eyes and in the eyes of all his servants.
Pharaoh said to his servants, 'Can we find a man like this, in whom there is a spirit of prophecy from before יְיָ?'
Pharaoh said to Yosef, 'Since יְיָ has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.'
'You shall be appointed over my house, and at your word all my people shall be fed. Only by this royal throne shall I be higher in honor than you.'
Pharaoh said to Yosef, 'See, I have appointed you over all the land of Egypt.'
Pharaoh removed his ring from his hand and placed it on Yosef's hand. He clothed him in garments of fine linen and placed a gold necklace around his neck.
He had him ride in his second chariot, and they proclaimed before him, 'This is a father to the king!' He appointed him over all the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh said to Yosef, 'I am Pharaoh, and without your word no man shall raise his hand to grasp a weapon or his foot to mount a horse in all the land of Egypt.'
Pharaoh called Yosef's name 'The man to whom hidden things are revealed.' He gave him אסנת, daughter of פוטי פרע, the chief of און, as a wife. Yosef went out (as ruler) over the land of Egypt.
Yosef was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Yosef went out from before Pharaoh and passed (as ruler) through all the land of Egypt.
During the seven years of plenty, the inhabitants of the land gathered grain into storehouses.
He gathered all the grain of the seven years that were in the land of Egypt and placed grain in the towns. The grain of the countryside surrounding each town he placed within it.
Yosef gathered grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until he stopped counting, for it was beyond counting.
Two sons were born to Yosef before the year of famine came, whom אסנת, daughter of פוטי פרע, the chief of און, bore to him.
Yosef called the firstborn's name Menasheh, 'For יְיָ has made me forget all my toil and all my father's house.'
He called the second one's name Efrayim, 'For יְיָ has made me fruitful in the land of my servitude.'
The seven years of plenty that had been in the land of Egypt came to an end.
The seven years of famine began to arrive, just as Yosef had said. There was famine in all the lands, but throughout the land of Egypt there was bread.
All the land of Egypt grew hungry, and the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, 'Go to Yosef; do whatever he tells you.'
The famine was over the whole face of the land. Yosef opened all the storehouses in which there was grain and sold to Egypt. The famine grew severe in the land of Egypt.
All the inhabitants of the land came into Egypt to buy grain from Yosef, because the famine was severe throughout the land.
He said, 'Behold, I have heard people saying that grain is being sold in Egypt. Go down there and buy for us from there, so that we may live and not die.'
Yosef's ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
Yaakov did not send Binyamin, Yosef's brother, with his brothers, for he said, 'Lest death befall him.'
The sons of Yisrael came to buy grain among those who were coming in, because there was famine in the land of Canaan.
Yosef was the ruler over the land; he was the one selling grain to all the people of the land. Yosef's brothers came and bowed to him with their faces to the ground.

Yosef saw his brothers and recognized them. He considered what he would say to them and spoke harshly with them. He said to them, 'Where have you come from?' They said, 'From the land of Canaan, to buy grain.'
Yosef recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
Yosef remembered the dreams that he had dreamed about them. He said to them, 'You are spies! You have come to see the land's vulnerable places.'
They said to him, 'No, my lord! Your servants have come in to buy grain.'
'We are all sons of one man. We are honest men; your servants have not been spies.'
He said to them, 'No! You have come to see the land's vulnerable places.'
They said, 'We, your servants, are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. Behold, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no longer here.'
Yosef said to them, 'It is just as I told you, saying, “You are spies!”'
'By this you shall be tested: by Pharaoh's life, you shall not leave here unless your youngest brother comes here.'
'Send one of you, and let him bring your brother, while you remain confined. Your words will be tested to see whether you are speaking the truth. If not, by Pharaoh's life, you are spies!'
He gathered them into custody for three days.
On the third day Yosef said to them, 'Do this and remain alive; I am in fear before יְיָ.'
'If you are honest men, let one of your brothers be confined in the place of your custody, while you go and carry the grain that is lacking in your households.'
'Bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be believed and you will not die.' They did so.

They said to one another, 'Truly, we are guilty concerning our brother: we saw the distress of his soul when he was pleading with us, and we did not heed him. That is why this distress has come upon us.'
Reuven answered them, saying, 'Did I not tell you, saying, “Do not sin against the youth,” but you did not heed me? And now his blood too is being demanded.'
They did not know that Yosef understood, because an interpreter was between them.
He turned away from them and wept. He returned to them and spoke with them, took Shimon away from them, and bound him before their eyes.

Yosef gave orders, and they filled their containers with grain; he also ordered that each man's money be returned to his sack and that provisions for the journey be given to them. He did this for them.
They loaded their grain onto their donkeys and went away from there.
One of them opened his sack to give fodder to his donkey at the lodging place. He saw his money, and behold, it was at the opening of his load.

He said to his brothers, 'My money has been returned, and look, it is in my load!' Understanding left their hearts, and they were bewildered, saying to one another, 'What is this that יְיָ has done to us?'
They came to Yaakov their father in the land of Canaan and told him everything that had happened to them, saying:
'The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly with us and treated us as spies of the land.'
'We said to him, “We are honest men; we have not been spies.”'
'“We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no longer here, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.”'
'The man who is lord of the land said to us, “By this I shall know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take the grain that is lacking in your households, and go.”'
'“Bring your youngest brother to me, and I shall know that you are not spies but honest men. I shall give your brother back to you, and you may conduct trade in the land.”'
As they were emptying their sacks, behold, each man's bundle of money was in his sack. They and their father saw their bundles of money and were afraid.
Yaakov their father said to them, 'You have bereaved me! Yosef is no longer here, Shimon is not here, and you would take Binyamin. All these things have come upon me.'
Reuven spoke to his father, saying, 'You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Entrust him to my hand, and I will return him to you.'
He said, 'My son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he alone remains. If death befalls him on the road you travel, you will bring my gray hair down in sorrow to Sheol.'
The famine was severe in the land.
When they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, 'Go back and buy us a little grain.'
Yehudah said to him, 'The man solemnly warned us, saying, “You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.”'
'If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy grain for you.'
'But if you will not send him, we will not go down, for the man said to us, “You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.”'
Yisrael said, 'Why did you do me harm by telling the man that you still had a brother?'

They said, 'The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family, saying, “Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?” We told him in response to these words. Could we possibly have known that he would say, “Bring your brother down”?'
Yehudah said to Yisrael his father, 'Send the youth with me, and let us arise and go, so that we may live and not die—we, you, and our little ones as well.'
'I will stand surety for him; you may demand him from my hand. If I do not bring him back to you and set him before you, I shall be sinning against you for all time.'
'For had we not delayed over this, by now we would have returned these two times.'
'Take twice as much money in your hands, and return in your hands the money that was put back at the openings of your loads; perhaps it was a mistake.'
'Take your brother, arise, and return to the man.'
The men took this gift, took twice as much money in their hands, and brought Binyamin. They arose, went down to Egypt, and stood before Yosef.
Yosef saw Binyamin with them and said to the man appointed over his house, 'Bring the men into the house, slaughter animals, and prepare, for the men will eat with me at the meal.'
The man did as Yosef had said, and the man brought the men into Yosef's house.

The men were afraid because they had been brought into Yosef's house. They said, 'We are being brought in on account of the money returned in our loads the first time, to lord it over us, to attack us, to acquire us as slaves, and to take our donkeys.'
They approached the man appointed over Yosef's house and spoke with him at the doorway of the house.
They said, 'Please, my lord! We did come down the first time to buy grain.'
'When we came to the lodging place and opened our loads, behold, each man's money was at the opening of his load—our money in its full weight. We have brought it back in our hands.'
'We have brought down other money in our hands to buy grain. We do not know who put our money in our loads.'
He said, 'Peace to you; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father gave you treasure in your loads. Your money came to me.' He brought Shimon out to them.
The man brought the men into Yosef's house and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave fodder to their donkeys.
They prepared the gift for Yosef's arrival at mealtime, because they had heard that they would eat bread there.
Yosef came into the house, and they brought him the gift that was in their hands into the house and bowed to him to the ground.
He asked them about their welfare and said, 'Is your elderly father, of whom you spoke, well? Is he still alive?'
They said, 'Your servant, our father, is well; he is still alive.' They knelt and bowed.
He raised his eyes and saw Binyamin his brother, his mother's son. He said, 'Is this your youngest brother, of whom you told me?' He said, 'May compassion be granted to you from before יְיָ, my son.'
Yosef hurried, for his compassion was stirred for his brother, and he wanted to weep. He entered the bedroom chamber and wept there.
He washed his face and came out, restrained himself, and said, 'Set out the bread.'
They reclined before him, the older according to his seniority and the younger according to his youth. The men looked at one another in amazement.
He took portions from before him and set them before them. Binyamin's portion was greater than the portions of any of them—five portions. They drank and became drunk with him.
He commanded the man appointed over his house, saying, 'Fill the men's loads with as much grain as they can carry, and put each man's money at the opening of his load.'
'Put my cup, the silver cup, at the opening of the youngest one's load, together with the money for his purchase.' He did according to the word Yosef had spoken.
Morning grew light, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

They had gone out of the town but had not gone far when Yosef said to the man appointed over his house, 'Arise, pursue the men, catch up with them, and say to them, “Why have you repaid evil in place of good?”'
He caught up with them and spoke these words to them.
They said to him, 'Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!'
'Whichever of your servants it is found with shall die, and we too shall become slaves to my lord.'
He said, 'Even now, it is as you have said: the one with whom it is found shall be my slave, and you shall be innocent.'
They hurried and each lowered his load to the ground, and each opened his load.
He searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest. The cup was found in Binyamin's load.
They tore their garments, each loaded his donkey, and they returned to the town.
Yehudah and his brothers entered Yosef's house, and he was still there. They fell to the ground before him.

Yehudah said, 'What shall we say to my lord? What shall we speak, and how shall we clear ourselves? From before יְיָ, guilt has been found in your servants. Behold, we are slaves to my lord, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found.'
He said, 'Far be it from me to do this! The man in whose hand the cup is found shall be my slave. But you, go up in peace to your father.'
'And just as he interpreted for us, so it happened: he restored me to my service, and he hung the other man up.'

qualifications.he: הניסוח האנגלי 'hung ... up' משמר את משמעות התלייה של צְלָב בלי לקבוע תלייה בחבל מן הצוואר, שיפוד או צורת קיבוע מסוימת. הפעלים הפעילים נשמרים, אך אין נוסף שם לנושא שאינו נקוב במשפט; אין לזהות את מבצע המעשים עם פותר החלומות רק בגלל רצף המשפטים.
qualifications.en: 'Hung ... up' retains the suspension expressed by צְלָב without specifying hanging by the neck, impalement, or a particular fastening method. The active verbs remain, but no name is supplied for their unstated subject; the sequence of clauses alone must not identify the agent of these acts with the dream interpreter.
qualifications.anchor: יָתִי אֲתֵיב עַל שִׁמּוּשִׁי וְיָתֵיהּ צְלָב

pairs.fullEnglish: 'Let Pharaoh act and appoint trustworthy officials over the land, and let him mobilize the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty.'

qualifications.he: 'Mobilize' מתאר זירוז והכנה של הארץ לקראת איסוף התבואה המפורט בהמשך. הניסוח אינו קובע מנגנון מנהלי מסוים ואינו מוסיף גביית חמישית, שאינה נאמרת במילים הארמיות האלה.
qualifications.en: 'Mobilize' expresses setting the land into activity and preparation for the grain collection described next. It does not specify an administrative mechanism or add a one-fifth levy, which these Aramaic words do not state.

pairs.fullEnglish: They set it out for him separately, for them separately, and for the Egyptians who ate with him separately. For the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, because the Hebrews eat the livestock that the Egyptians worship.
'“Is this not the cup from which my lord drinks and with which he makes thorough investigation? You have done evil in what you have done.”'

qualifications.he: הצירוף הארמי מדגיש בדיקה או חקירה; בֵּיהּ שבמשפט קושר אותה לכוס. אין במילים האלה פירוט של אופן הבדיקה. זהו נוסח ההאשמה שיוסף מורה למסור באמצעות הממונה על ביתו, ולא עדות נפרדת למעשה ניחוש שהתרחש. התרגום 'makes thorough investigation' משמר זאת ואינו מחליף את לשון אונקלוס בפועל אחר מן הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: The Aramaic construction emphasizes examining or investigating; the sentence's בֵּיהּ connects it with the cup. These words do not specify the procedure. This is the accusation Yosef instructs his household appointee to deliver, not independent evidence that an act of divination occurred. 'Makes thorough investigation' preserves that wording rather than replacing Onkelos's verb with a different verb from the Hebrew verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yosef said to them, 'What is this deed you have done? Did you not know that a man like me makes thorough investigation?'

qualifications.he: הצירוף מדגיש בדיקה או חקירה. כאן יוסף אומר שאדם כמותו חוקר היטב; בניגוד למד:ה, המשפט הזה אינו מוסיף בֵּיהּ ואינו נוקב בכוס או באמצעי החקירה. הקשר ההאשמה נשמר, אך אין להוסיף לגוף המשפט שיטת ניחוש או לראות בדבריו עדות עצמאית למעשה כזה.
qualifications.en: The construction emphasizes examining or investigating. Here Yosef says that a man like him investigates thoroughly; unlike 44:5, this sentence adds no בֵּיהּ and names neither a cup nor a means of inquiry. The accusation's context is retained, but no divinatory procedure should be inserted into the body or treated as independently established by this speech.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yaakov saw that grain was being sold in Egypt. Yaakov said to his sons, 'Why do you show yourselves?'

qualifications.he: תִּתְחֲזוּן ניתן להבנה חוזרת, ׳מדוע אתם מראים את עצמכם?׳, או להבנה הדדית, ׳מדוע אתם מביטים זה בזה?׳. גוף התרגום משקף את הראשונה. המשפט אינו נוקב במושא או בטעם לשאלה; אין להוסיף הצגת עושר, מחסור או מבוכה כאילו נאמרו בו.
qualifications.en: תִּתְחֲזוּן allows a reflexive understanding, ‘Why do you show yourselves?’, or a reciprocal understanding, ‘Why do you look at one another?’ The body reflects the first. The clause specifies neither an object nor a motive; it does not expressly say that they display wealth, want, or perplexity.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘Behold, the money we found at the openings of our loads we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord's house?’

qualifications.he: הנוסח הראשי אומר 'כסף או זהב'. ההמשך המוסגר במקור הוא 'מָנִין דִּכְסַף אוֹ מָנִין דִּדְהָב', כלומר כלי כסף או כלי זהב. שני הניסוחים מוצגים, בלי להכריע שהנוסח המצומצם לכלים הוא הנוסח היחיד ובלי להוסיף סוג כלי מסוים.
qualifications.en: The main wording says 'silver or gold'. The source's parenthesized wording is 'מָנִין דִּכְסַף אוֹ מָנִין דִּדְהָב', silver vessels or gold vessels. Both are presented without making the narrower vessel wording the sole reading or adding a particular kind of vessel.

pairs.fullEnglish: Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the Ark of the Covenant of ייָ. He offered up burnt offerings, slaughtered sacred sacrifices, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women who were innkeepers came to seek judgment before the king, and they stood before him.
One woman said, ‘Please, my lord: this woman and I live in one house, and I gave birth while she was with me in the house.
This woman’s son died during the night because she lay upon him.
She arose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant was asleep. She laid him beside herself, and she laid her dead son beside me.’
Listen to discipline and become wise; do not trample it underfoot.
Happy is the person who listens to me and keeps watch at my thresholds each and every day, guarding the doorposts of the gate.
For whoever finds me finds life, and favor shall be his from before אֱלָהָא.
But whoever sins against me destroys his own soul, and all who hate me love death.
Wisdom built her house and set seven pillars in it.
She slaughtered the animals for her feast, mixed her wine, and arranged her table.
‘I arose in the morning to nurse my son, and behold, he was dead. I looked closely at him in the morning, and behold, he was not my son whom I had borne.’

The other woman said, ‘Not so! My son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.’ And this woman said to that woman, ‘Not so! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’ They disputed before the king.
The king said, ‘This woman says, “This living one is my son, and your son is the dead one”; and this woman says, “Not so! Your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.”’
The king said, ‘Bring me a sword.’ They brought a sword before the king.
‘Whoever is simple, let him come to me.’ To the one lacking understanding she said:
‘Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine that I have mixed.
Put away from yourselves your lack of understanding, and live; walk in the path of discernment.’
The king said, ‘Cut the living child into two pieces, and give half to one woman and half to the other.’

The woman whose son was the living one spoke to the king, for her compassion was stirred for her son. She said, ‘Please, my lord, give her the living child, and certainly do not kill him!’ But the other woman said, ‘Let him be neither mine nor yours. Cut him apart!’
The king answered and said, ‘Give her the living child, and certainly do not kill him. She is his mother.’
All Israel heard the judgment that the king had rendered, and they stood in fear before the king, for they saw that wisdom from before יְיָ was within him to administer judgment.
King Solomon was king over all Israel.
Whoever disciplines a scoffer receives disgrace for himself, and rebuking a wicked person is a blemish to the one who rebukes him.
Do not rebuke a scoffer, lest he hate you. Rebuke a wise person, so that he may love you.
Teach a wise person, and he will become still wiser. Give knowledge to a righteous person, and he will increase in knowledge.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of אֱלָהָא, and knowledge of the holy ones is discernment.
For through her your days will become many, and years of life will be added to you.
אֱלִיחוֹרֶף and אֲחִיָה, sons of שִׁישָׁא, were the scribes; יְהוֹשָׁפָט son of אֲחִילוּד was appointed over the records;
בְנָיָהוּ son of יְהוֹיָדָע was appointed over the army; צָדוֹק and אֶבְיָתָר were the priests;
עֲזַרְיָהוּ son of נָתָן was appointed over the governors; זָבוּד son of נָתָן was a high official, the king’s close companion;
אֲחִישָׁר was appointed over the household; אֲדֹנִירָם son of עַבְרָא was appointed over those who collect taxes.
Solomon had twelve governors appointed over all Israel, who supplied provisions for the king and the members of his household. Each one’s turn to supply provisions was one month in the year.
If you have become wise, you have become wise for yourself; but if you become a scoffer, you alone will bear the burden.
She sits at the entrance of her house, on a high and sturdy seat.
She calls to those passing along the road whose paths are straight:
For whoever is simple, let him come to her; and to the one lacking understanding she says:
‘Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in concealment is pleasant.’
These were their names: the son of חוּר, in the hill country of the house of Ephraim;
the son of דֶקֶר, in מָקַץ, in שַׁעֲלַבִים, in בֵית שָׁמֶשׁ, and in אֵלוֹן belonging to בֵית חָנָן;
the son of חֶסֶד, in אֲרֻבּוֹת; סוֹכוֹ and all the land of חֵפֶר belonged to his charge;
the son of אֲבִינָדָב, over all the districts of דֹאר; טָפַת, Solomon’s daughter, was his wife;

בַּעֲנָא son of אֲחִילוּד, over תַּעֲנָךְ, מְגִידוֹ, and all בֵּית שְׁאָן, which is beside צָרְתָנָה below יִזְרְעֶאל, from בֵּית שְׁאָן as far as the plain of מְחוֹלָה, as far as the other side of יָקְמְעָם.
The proverbs of Solomon: a wise son will gladden his father, but a foolish son embitters his mother.
The treasures of a wicked person bring no benefit, but righteousness rescues from an evil death.
אֱלָהָא does not let the soul of the righteous person go hungry, but He will sweep away the possessions of the wicked.
He does not know that she has brought men down there, and that all those invited to her are in the depths of the underworld.
She sent her maidens to call out upon the crest of the strong, guarded heights.
Poverty brings the idle man low, but a diligent hand makes them rich.

qualifications.he: לְהוֹן הוא כינוי רבים, ולכן הוא מתורגם ׳אותם׳ גם לאחר הגבר היחיד שבמשפט הראשון. המקור אינו מציין כאן קבוצה מסוימת שאליה חוזר הכינוי; שמירת הרבים אינה מזהה קבוצה ואינה מתקנת את המקור ליחיד.
qualifications.en: לְהוֹן is plural and is therefore rendered 'them,' even after the single man in the first clause. The source does not identify a particular group as the pronoun's referent here; preserving the plural neither identifies such a group nor emends the source to a singular object.

pairs.fullEnglish: These were his high officials: עֲזַרְיָהוּ son of צָדוֹק, the priest;

qualifications.he: כַּהֲנָא פירושו ׳הכוהן׳. התואר בא לאחר כל הצירוף עֲזַרְיָהוּ בַר צָדוֹק; התרגום האנגלי שומר על סדר זה ואינו מכריע בפני עצמו אם התואר מוסב על עזריהו או על צדוק. אין להחליף את תואר הכהונה בתואר ממשלתי כדי להסיר את שאלת הסמיכות.
qualifications.en: כַּהֲנָא means 'the priest.' The title follows the whole phrase עֲזַרְיָהוּ בַר צָדוֹק; the English preserves that sequence without independently deciding whether the title attaches to עֲזַרְיָהוּ or צָדוֹק. The priestly title is not replaced with a government office to remove the attachment question.

pairs.fullEnglish: 'May אֵל שַׁדַּי grant you compassion before the man, so that he releases your other brother and Binyamin to you. And as for me, as I have been bereaved, so I am bereaved.'

qualifications.he: ההשוואה והחזרה על השכול נשמרות: כשם שכבר שָׁכַל, כך הוא מקבל את מצב שכולו. תְּכֵלִית אינה נקראת כאן כהבטחה בלשון עתיד שאובדן נוסף יתרחש; סיומת ית שייכת לצורה האישית שבמשפט החוזר. ההקשר הוא השלמה בשעה ששולחים בן נוסף, ולא ידיעה על מותו. דברי רש״י ׳עַד שׁוּבְכֶם אֶהְיֶה שַׁכּוּל מִסָּפֵק׳ מסייעים להבנת ההקשר, אך שמות הבנים שהוא מונה בפירושו אינם נוספים לגוף התרגום.
qualifications.en: The comparison and repeated bereavement are preserved: as he has already been bereaved, so he accepts his bereaved condition. תְּכֵלִית is not read here as a future assurance that another loss will occur; its final ית belongs to the personal form in the repeated clause. The context is resignation while another son is sent away, not knowledge of his death. Rashi's עַד שׁוּבְכֶם אֶהְיֶה שַׁכּוּל מִסָּפֵק supports that contextual distinction, but the sons he names in his exposition are not added to the translation body.

pairs.fullEnglish: ‘And behold, seven ears of grain, empty of grain, blighted and battered by the east wind, sprouted after them.’

qualifications.he: ׳ריקות מגרעינים׳ מוסר את תיאור נָצָן בנפרד מתיאורי הפגיעה שאחריו. רש״י מסביר כאן במפורש את התרגום: ׳אין בהם אלא הנץ, לפי שנתרוקנו מן הזרע׳. אין הכוונה לשיבולים תקינות המצויות רק בשלב הפריחה.
qualifications.en: 'Empty of grain' renders נָצָן separately from the following damage descriptions. Rashi expressly explains the Targum here: only the blossom remains because the grain has emptied out. The description is not of healthy ears merely at the flowering stage.

pairs.fullEnglish: Yisrael their father said to them, ‘If it must be so, do this: take some of what is prized in the land in your containers, and bring down a gift to the man—a little balsam and a little honey, wax and aromatic resin, nuts and almonds.’

qualifications.he: קְטַף נמסר כצרי, כלומר הפרשה צמחית ריחנית; שְׁעַף כשעווה; לְטוֹם כשרף ריחני; ובָּטְנִין כאגוזים במובן של פירות אגוזיים, בלי לקבוע מין בוטני. אלו משמעויות של שמות המוצרים הארמיים, ולא זיהוי של מין עץ, מקור השעווה, הרכב השרף או מין האגוזים. דְּבַשׁ ושִׁגְדִין הם דבש ושקדים. שני מופעי זְעֵיר מוסבים על הצרי ועל הדבש בהתאמה. רש״י מייחס במפורש לאונקלוס פירוש של שעווה בפירושו לבראשית לז:כה. לעומת זאת, פירוש השורש הצמחי שהוא מביא שם למילה העברית לט אינו הגדרה מפורשת של לְטוֹם הארמית. על בטנים שבפסוק העברי הוא אומר כאן ׳לא ידעתי מה הם׳, ובהמשך מביא זיהוי בשם אחרים והשוואה מסויגת משלו. אי־ידיעתו נשמרת כלשונה: התרגום הכללי ׳אגוזים׳ אינו מוצג כזיהוי של רש״י, ואין בו הכרעה שהמוצר ההיסטורי היה פיסטוקים ממין מסוים.
qualifications.en: קְטַף is rendered balsam, an aromatic plant exudate; שְׁעַף, wax; לְטוֹם, aromatic resin; and בָּטְנִין, nuts in the ordinary sense of nut-like fruits, without fixing a botanical species. These render the Aramaic product names, not a tree species, the source of the wax, the resin's composition, or a nut species. דְּבַשׁ and שִׁגְדִין are honey and almonds. The two occurrences of זְעֵיר qualify balsam and honey respectively. In his comment on Genesis 37:25, Rashi expressly attributes a wax rendering to Onkelos. By contrast, the plant-root explanation he reports there for Hebrew לט is not an explicit definition of Aramaic לְטוֹם. Of Hebrew בטנים here he says, ‘I do not know what they are,’ then reports another identification and offers a tentative comparison of his own. His uncertainty stands as stated: the broad rendering nuts is not presented as Rashi's identification and does not determine that the historical product was a particular pistachio species.
qualifications.anchor: קְטַף וּזְעֵיר דְּבַשׁ שְׁעַף וּלְטוֹם בָּטְנִין וְשִׁגְדִין

pairs.fullEnglish: A foolish and roaming woman is simple-minded and knows nothing good.

qualifications.he: פְרִידְתָּא מתארת כאן אישה היוצאת ומסתובבת לבדה. זהו התיאור שיסטרוב קושר במפורש לפסוק, באמצעות המילה פַּרְדָּנִית. אין זו רק אמירה כללית על מרדנות, ואין התיאור כשלעצמו מספר על מעשה מסוים או על תוצאותיו.
qualifications.en: פְרִידְתָּא here describes a woman who goes out and about on her own. This is the description Jastrow expressly connects with the verse through the equivalent פַּרְדָּנִית. It is not merely a general description of rebelliousness, nor does it by itself narrate a particular incident or its consequences.

qualifications.he: שִׁבְרָתָה מובנת כתיאור בנקבה, במשמעות פתיה או חסרת דעת, הנאמר על אותה אישה. יסטרוב מביא את הצורה הזאת עצמה כקריאת וילנה בפסוק. הה״א האחרונה אינה מציינת כאן שייכות של דבר אחר לאישה. התיאור אינו קובע את גילה; ההמשך אומר שהיא אינה יודעת טוב, ולא רק שאינה יודעת דבר מסוים שלא פורש.
qualifications.en: שִׁבְרָתָה is understood as a feminine description, simple or foolish, predicated of the same woman. Jastrow records this very form as the Wilna reading of the verse. Its final ה does not here make another thing her possession. The description does not establish her age; the following clause says that she knows nothing good, not merely that she lacks unspecified knowledge.

dayTitle.en: Two Dreams of Plenty and Blight

explanation.he: הקריאה מציגה את חלום הפרות ואת תחילת חלום השיבולים. אונקלוס מציין שהפרות הרזות עומדות מול הפרות האחרות על שפת הנהר, ומתאר את השיבולים האחרונות כלקויות וכמוכות רוח קדים.
explanation.en: The reading presents the dream of the cows and the beginning of the dream of the grain. Onkelos places the lean cows opposite the others on the riverbank and describes the later ears as blighted and battered by the east wind.

dayTitle.he: רוח פרעה נטרפת ושר המשקים נזכר
dayTitle.en: Pharaoh Is Agitated and the Chief Cupbearer Remembers

explanation.he: בליעת השיבולים מסיימת את החלום השני, אך חכמי מצרים אינם נותנים לפרעה פתרון. התרגום מתאר את רוחו כטרופה, ולאחר מכן מעביר את הדיבור לשר המשקים, המזכיר את חטאיו ואת מאסרו עם שר האופים בבית רב הטבחים.
explanation.en: The swallowing of the ears ends the second dream, but Egypt's wise men provide Pharaoh with no interpretation. The Targum describes his spirit as agitated, then turns to the chief cupbearer's account of his offenses and his confinement with the chief baker in the chief executioner's house.

dayTitle.he: עדות שר המשקים והוצאת יוסף מבית האסורים
dayTitle.en: The Cupbearer's Testimony and Yosef's Release from Prison

explanation.he: שר המשקים מעיד שכל אחד משני החלומות קיבל פתרון משלו, ושהמאורעות התאימו לפתרון. פרעה מזמן את יוסף מבית האסורים; אונקלוס מציין שיוסף מסתפר ומחליף את לבושו לפני כניסתו. פרעה מציג לו את החלום הבלתי פתור ואת מה ששמע על יכולתו לפרשו.
explanation.en: The chief cupbearer testifies that each dream received its own interpretation and that events matched it. Pharaoh summons Yosef from prison; Onkelos notes his haircut and change of clothing before his entrance. Pharaoh presents his unresolved dream and what he has heard about Yosef's ability to interpret.

dayTitle.he: לא מחכמת יוסף: פרעה מספר על הפרות
dayTitle.en: Not from Yosef's Wisdom: Pharaoh Recounts the Cows

explanation.he: יוסף שולל את ייחוס המענה לחכמתו, ומייחס את המענה לשלום פרעה למה שיינתן מלפני יי. בסיפור פרעה נזכרים גם דלות הפרות וגם מראיהן הרע במיוחד. הבליעה אינה משנה את מראיהן, ולכן אין ניכר שהפרות השמנות נכנסו למעיהן.
explanation.en: Yosef denies that the answer comes from his wisdom and attributes the answer for Pharaoh's welfare to what will be given from before יְיָ. Pharaoh's account emphasizes both the cows' scrawniness and their exceptional ugliness. Swallowing leaves their appearance unchanged, so there is no visible indication that the fat cows entered their bellies.

dayTitle.en: The Two Visions Are One Dream

explanation.he: פרעה מספר כיצד השיבולים הלקויות בולעות את השיבולים הטובות, ומדגיש שהחרטומים לא ביארו לו את החלום. יוסף מגדיר את חלום פרעה כאחד ומקשר הן את שבע הפרות הטובות והן את שבע השיבולים הטובות לשבע שנים. ההודעה לפרעה עוסקת במה שיי עתיד לעשות.
explanation.en: Pharaoh recounts how the blighted ears swallow the good ones and stresses that the sorcerers have not explained the dream. Yosef calls Pharaoh's dream one and identifies both the seven good cows and the seven good ears with seven years. What is being made known to Pharaoh concerns what יְיָ is going to do.

dayTitle.he: פתרון החלום, אגירת התבואה ומינוי יוסף
dayTitle.en: The Dream Explained, Grain Stored, and Yosef Appointed

explanation.he: יוסף מפרש את שנות השובע והרעב ומסביר שכפילות החלום מעידה שהדבר מוכן מלפני יי. הצעתו כוללת מינוי נאמנים וזירוז הארץ לקראת אגירת תבואה בערים, ופרעה מכיר בו כבעל רוח נבואה מלפני יי. אונקלוס מפרט את סמכותו בדבר הזנת העם, אחיזת נשק ורכיבה על סוס, ומפרש את השם החדש כתיאור אדם שהנסתרות גלויות לו. בקריאת שמות בניו יוסף מייחס ליי את השכחת כל עמלו וכל בית אביו ואת הפרייתו בארץ שעבודו.
explanation.en: Yosef interprets the years of plenty and famine and explains that the repeated dream means the matter is established from before יְיָ. His proposal includes trustworthy officials and mobilizing the land for grain reserves in the towns, and Pharaoh recognizes in him a spirit of prophecy from before יְיָ. Onkelos specifies his authority over feeding the people, taking up weapons, and mounting horses, and renders his new name as a man to whom hidden things are revealed. In naming his sons, Yosef attributes to יְיָ both his forgetting all his toil and all his father's house and his fruitfulness in the land of his servitude.

dayTitle.he: מן הרעב אל סעודת האחים ופרשת הכוס
dayTitle.en: From Famine to the Brothers' Meal and the Affair of the Cup

explanation.he: הרעב מביא את האחים אל יוסף, המכיר אותם, שוקל את דבריו ובוחן את אמיתות דבריהם באמצעות הבאת האח הצעיר. הם מודים באשמתם כלפי אחיהם, ולאחר החזרת הכסף ושיבת שמעון הם אוכלים בבית יוסף עם בנימין. אונקלוס מסביר את הפרדת המצרים מן העברים באכילת בעלי החיים שהמצרים עובדים להם, ומציין את חלקו המוגדל של בנימין. מציאת הכוס מוליכה להודאת יהודה באשמה שנמצאה מלפני יי, אך יוסף מגביל את העבדות לאדם שבידו נמצאה הכוס.
explanation.en: Famine brings the brothers to Yosef, who recognizes them, considers his words, and tests their truthfulness by requiring the youngest brother's arrival. They acknowledge their guilt toward their brother, and after the returned money and Shimon's release they eat in Yosef's house with Binyamin. Onkelos explains the separation of Egyptians and Hebrews by the Hebrews' eating animals the Egyptians worship, and notes Binyamin's enlarged portion. The cup's discovery leads to Yehudah's acknowledgment of guilt found from before יְיָ, but Yosef restricts slavery to the man in whose possession the cup was found.

dayTitle.en: Listening to Wisdom and the Preparation of Her Table

explanation.he: תרגום משלי מציג את החכמה כמי שקוראת לשמוע מוסר ולשקוד על פתחיה בכל יום. מציאתה נקשרת לחיים ולרצון מלפני אֱלָהָא, והקטע מסתיים בביתה בעל שבעת העמודים ובהכנת סעודתה.
explanation.en: The Targum of Proverbs presents Wisdom as calling people to listen to discipline and keep watch at her entrances every day. Finding her is associated with life and favor from before אֱלָהָא, and the reading ends with her seven-pillared house and the preparation of her feast.

dayTitle.he: הכרת הילד וטענות האימהות לפני המלך
dayTitle.en: Recognizing the Child and the Mothers’ Claims before the King

explanation.he: האישה מספרת שבבדיקת הילד בבוקר הכירה שאין זה הבן שילדה. התרגום מביא את הטענות הסותרות של שתי הנשים, את חזרת המלך על דבריהן ואת פקודתו להביא חרב.
explanation.en: The woman recounts how her close examination of the child in the morning showed that he was not the son she had borne. The Targum gives the women’s opposing claims, the king’s restatement of them, and his command to bring a sword.

dayTitle.en: Wisdom’s Invitation to Bread and the Path of Discernment

explanation.he: החכמה שולחת את נערותיה לקרוא ומזמינה את הפתי ואת חסר ההבנה לבוא אליה. הזמנתה כוללת לחם ויין שמזגה, ועזיבת חסרון ההבנה כדי לחיות וללכת בדרך הבינה.
explanation.en: Wisdom sends her maidens to call out and invites the simple and those lacking understanding to come to her. Her invitation includes bread and the wine she has mixed, together with leaving deficient understanding behind in order to live and walk in the path of discernment.

dayTitle.en: The Mother’s Compassion and Wisdom to Administer Judgment

explanation.he: ההוראה לחלק את הילד מגלה את רחמי אמו, המבקשת שיינתן לאחרת ובלבד שלא ייהרג. המלך מצווה לשמור את הילד בחיים ולהשיבו לאמו, וכל ישראל מכירים בחכמה שמלפני יְיָ שבקרבו לעשות דין.
explanation.en: The command to divide the child reveals his mother’s compassion: she asks that he be given to the other woman rather than killed. The king orders that the child be kept alive and given to his mother, and all Israel recognize the wisdom from before יְיָ within him for administering judgment.

dayTitle.en: Rebuke, Wisdom, and the Fear of אֱלָהָא

explanation.he: תרגום משלי מבחין בין תגובת הלץ לתוכחה ובין תגובת החכם, היכול לאהוב את מוכיחו ולהוסיף דעת. יראת אֱלָהָא מוצגת כראשית החכמה, ולחכמה נקשרים ריבוי ימים ותוספת שנות חיים.
explanation.en: The Targum of Proverbs contrasts the scoffer’s response to rebuke with that of the wise person, who can love the one who corrects him and gain further knowledge. Fear of אֱלָהָא is presented as the beginning of wisdom, and wisdom is associated with many days and added years of life.

dayTitle.he: שרי שלמה והממונים על כלכלת ביתו
dayTitle.en: Solomon’s Officials and Those Appointed to Provision His Household

explanation.he: תרגום הנביא מונה את בעלי התפקידים בממלכת שלמה, ובהם הסופרים, הממונה על הזיכרונות, הממונה על הצבא והכוהנים. הוא מפרט גם תפקידי ממשל, בית ומסים, ואת שנים עשר הממונים שכל אחד מהם מכלכל את המלך וביתו חודש בשנה.
explanation.en: The prophetic Targum lists the officeholders in Solomon’s kingdom, including the scribes, the official over the records, the official over the army, and the priests. It also describes government, household, and tax responsibilities, and the twelve governors, each of whom provisions the king and his household for one month of the year.

dayTitle.en: Personal Responsibility and the Foolish Woman’s Call

explanation.he: הקטע פותח בהבחנה בין החכמה המועילה לאדם עצמו ובין הליצנות שאת משאה יישא לבדו. לאחר מכן מתוארת אישה סכלה היושבת בפתח ביתה וקוראת לעוברים בדרך ישרה, תוך שבח למים גנובים וללחם הנאכל בסתר.
explanation.en: The reading begins by contrasting wisdom that benefits the person who acquires it with scoffing whose burden that person must bear alone. It then describes a foolish woman sitting at her doorway and calling to those following straight paths, praising stolen waters and bread eaten in concealment.

dayTitle.en: The Governors’ Names and the Extent of Their Responsibilities

explanation.he: תרגום הנביא ממשיך למנות את הממונים ואת המקומות הנתונים לאחריותם, מהר בית אפרים ועד מחוזות דור ואזור בית שאן. בתוך הרשימה נזכר גם הקשר המשפחתי של בן אבינדב לשלמה, שטפת בת המלך הייתה אשתו.
explanation.en: The prophetic Targum continues the list of governors and the places under their responsibility, from the hill country of the house of Ephraim to the districts of דֹאר and the area of בֵּית שְׁאָן. The list also records the family connection of the son of אֲבִינָדָב to Solomon: the king’s daughter טָפַת was his wife.

dayTitle.he: סופה של הזמנה רעה וראשית משלי שלמה
dayTitle.en: The End of an Evil Invitation and the Beginning of Solomon’s Proverbs

explanation.he: הקטע חותם את הזמנת האישה הסכלה בתיאור האורחים שבמעמקי השאול. אחר כך מתחילים משלי שלמה בניגודים שבין בן חכם לבן סכל, בין אוצרות הרשע לצדקה ובין רפיון לעמל מוכשר.
explanation.en: The reading closes the foolish woman’s invitation with a description of her guests in the depths of the underworld. Solomon’s proverbs then begin with contrasts between a wise and a foolish son, wicked wealth and righteousness, and idleness and diligent work.

dayTitle.he: החלום ובואן של שתי בעלות האכסניה לדין
dayTitle.en: The Dream and the Two Innkeepers’ Appearance for Judgment

explanation.he: תרגום הנביא מתאר את יקיצת שלמה, את הקרבנות ואת המשתה לעבדיו. אחר כך באות שתי נשים בעלות אכסניה לדין, ואחת מהן מספרת על הלידות, על מות הבן ועל החלפת הילדים בלילה.
explanation.en: The prophetic Targum describes Solomon’s awakening, his offerings, and the feast for his servants. Two women who are innkeepers then come for judgment, and one recounts the births, the death of a son, and the exchange of the children during the night.
